newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine merges nuclear body into new Energy Ministry.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine merges nuclear body into new Energy Ministry.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma has folded the state nuclear regulatory agency into the Energy and Electricity ministry, which has been renamed the Energy Ministry, the presidential press service said on Wednesday.
Energy and Electricity Minister Yuri Bochkarev was given the expanded portfolio and re-appointed Energy Minister, it said in a statement which added Kuchma had signed the decree on Tuesday.
The move is "to improve the governing structures in the energy-industrial complex and its efficiency", the statement said.
An Energy Ministry spokesman told Reuters Ukraine wanted to increase its electricity exports.
Last year Ukraine exported eight per cent of electricity production to Turkey, Bulgaria, Hungary and Poland.
It produced 300 billion kilowatt hours per year, a 30 percent decrease on 1990 output.
The former state nuclear authority, Derzhkomatom, will become an Energy ministry department and oversee safety at the five nuclear power plants which produce 45 per cent of Ukraine's electricity.
The Chernobyl nuclear power plant, which produces five per cent of Ukraine's power, was the site of the world's worst nuclear accident eleven years ago.
Forty-one conventional thermal plants produce 50 percent of Ukraine's electricity and six ageing hyrdoelectric stations produce about five percent.
